answer: Agents can join under pseudonyms, but an economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable deposit before it may vote on payments. A cedar-market agent, a glacier-route agent, and a raven-broker agent each face the same rule: identities that collude to claim rewards risk forfeiting their deposits when fraud is proven. Creating more names does not create more voting power; the attacker must tie up real capital per identity and can lose it, making a Sybil swarm expensive rather than merely a matter of generating accounts.
